title: Robot
description: A mechanism: a tree of rigid links connected by joints, driven by actuators. Structurally URDF rather than a Denavit-Hartenberg table, because DH has two incompatible conventions in common use and four columns do not record which one they are (ADR-0005). Note what is absent: there is no reach field (ADR-0003) and no payload field (ADR-0004). Both are derived, per-pose, and carry the assumptions that make them true.

make.description: Manufacturer, for a commercial mechanism. Absent for an original design.

kind.description: A LABEL for what sort of mechanism this is. It is not a topology constraint — that job belonged to this field until ADR-0008 found it contradicting the joints rule below, and now belongs solely to the tree check. Delta arms, four-bar linkages and Stewart platforms are true closed loops that the tree cannot express and are still absent rather than approximated; a joint COUPLED to another (a parallel jaw, a differential) is expressible as a mimic and is not a loop.

base_link.description: link_id of the root. The frame every transform in this record is ultimately relative to, and the frame every derived answer is relative to (ADR-0009). ClawBot does not model where this frame is in the world: a world pose comes from a localization stack, which is Oh-Ben-Claw's competence, and an answer claiming world coordinates would be asserting a pose with no source. A base that MOVES is expressible — give it a floating or planar joint — and reachability stays meaningful because it was never a world claim.

joints.description: May be empty only for a single-link record. Each joint names a parent and child link_id; the graph must be a tree rooted at base_link, which a validator checks — the schema cannot.

tool.description: The end effector and, more importantly, its offset. A reachability answer is meaningless without the tool offset it assumed, so the verdict carries it (ADR-0003). Null means no tool, which is a declaration, not an omission.

attached_to.description: link_id of the flange this tool bolts to. Defaults to the leaf link.

mass_g.description: A tool's own mass consumes payload capacity before any workpiece does.

measured_payload.description: Only ever figures somebody measured, each naming the pose it was measured at. There is deliberately no scalar payload field: rated capacity falls with extension because load torque is force times moment arm, so one number is true at one configuration and silently wrong everywhere else (ADR-0004). Absent means capacity is derived from continuous actuator torque, or not answered at all.

pose_rad.description: joint_id -> joint value at which the measurement was taken. Radians for revolute joints, millimetres for prismatic ones (the field name follows the dominant case; a validator checks per joint type).

how_measured.description: What was lifted, held for how long, judged by what. A figure with no method behind it is indistinguishable from a recalled one.

sustained.description: Whether the load was held long enough for the actuators to reach thermal steady state. A mass lifted once is not a mass the mechanism can hold.

policy.description: The author's declaration of policy categories under Project BINGO's shared taxonomy (platform decision PD-5, ClawBot ADR-0019). OPTIONAL, and absent means UNDECLARED — which ClawBot will not convert into 'none' on your behalf, because BINGO reads an absent declaration AS a 'none' declaration carrying fraud consequences. The consequence of leaving it absent is narrow and specific: manifest.py --as-project refuses to emit, because that document is bound for a network that requires a declaration. Every derivation - fk, reach, hold, can_it - runs regardless; computing kinematics is not fabricating, and a repo that refused to multiply matrices would be theatre. ClawBot NEVER INFERS a category from geometry, link lengths or a name; the declaration is the author's and only the author's.

categories.description: Category ids verbatim from BINGO's REFUSAL-CATEGORIES spec, e.g. 'none', 'regulated.medical', 'weapons.other'. Stored as strings and DELIBERATELY NOT validated against a hardcoded enum: that would fork a taxonomy whose own spec says growth requires a spec revision, and a forked registry that drifts is the failure OpenPartsCore exists to end. BINGO adjudicates; this repo carries the declaration faithfully.

taxonomy_version.description: REQUIRED whenever categories are present. A category id without the version of the list it came from is a string whose meaning lives somewhere else - the same defect ADR-0005 rejects DH parameters for. BINGO freezes this file's hash into a job at order time; record whatever identifies the list you declared against.

declared_by.description: Who made this declaration. It is a claim a person makes, not a measurement, so it has an author rather than a method.

note.description: Prose. A vendor's published reach figure belongs here if it is worth recording at all — as prose a human reads, never as a field a consumer could mistake for a derived answer (ADR-0003).

link.description: A rigid body. Exactly one of part_id, make or provenance_ref, mirroring OpenBuildCore's three requirement kinds so the vocabularies do not diverge (ADR-0006).

part_id.description: A part from OpenPartsCore. Stored, not resolved: a consumer needing its mass reads the registry. ClawBot imports nothing (ADR-0006).

make.description: Something fabricated rather than bought. Fields match OpenBuildCore's make requirement (its ADR-0006) so a robot's bill of made parts can be handed to its machine check without translation. This is declared design intent, not a measurement.

material.description: Lowercase token, e.g. pla, petg, asa, alu-6061. Required: a made part with no material cannot be checked against a machine at all, and defaulting would invent a design decision on the author's behalf.

provenance_ref.description: An OpenDesignCore artifact. The strongest of the three kinds: the geometry exists, so bbox and volume are facts rather than intent. Same distinction OBC drew between a project's declared size and can-print --from-sidecar.

schema.description: e.g. odc/provenance/0.2 — recorded so a record too old to carry bbox_mm is refused with its schema named rather than silently falling back.

mass_g.description: Only for a link whose mass is not obtainable from its part_id or provenance record. Needed for a static payload derivation; absent means that derivation reports incomplete rather than assuming zero.

type.description: URDF's vocabulary, all six of it. revolute has limits; continuous rotates without them; prismatic slides; fixed is a rigid attachment that exists to carry a transform; floating has six degrees of freedom; planar moves in a plane. The enum carried four until ADR-0009 — which meant 'structurally URDF' was already false by omission, before anyone asked for a mobile base. floating and planar say the base MOVES; they do not say how, and wheels, propellers, odometry and gait are not modelled here.

axis.description: Axis of rotation or translation in the child frame. Required for every type but fixed; a validator enforces that, and also that it is not the zero vector.

limits.description: Absent or null means UNKNOWN, never unlimited. A reachability computation over a joint with no limits answers 'incomplete' and names this joint (ADR-0003), because assuming full travel claims points the mechanism cannot reach. Note what this costs at the URDF boundary: urdfdom REFUSES to parse a revolute or prismatic joint with no limit element, so a record in exactly this honest state has no valid URDF representation and export must fail naming the joint rather than emit a zero (ADR-0007). A floating or planar joint has no meaningful limits and a validator must not demand them — its travel is bounded by an environment, and this repo does not model environments (ADR-0009).

lower_rad.description: Revolute joints. Bounded at +/- 4*pi deliberately: radians are hostile to hand-authoring and a typed 90 in a _rad field is a plausible mistake, so the range check is the main defence ADR-0005 leaves standing.

effort_nm.description: Maximum torque the joint may be commanded to produce. Distinct from the actuator's continuous torque: this is a limit imposed on the mechanism, that one is what the motor can sustain. A capacity derivation takes the lesser.

actuator_id.description: The actuator driving this joint, from data/actuators/. Absent for a fixed joint, and for a joint moved by hand.

gear_ratio.description: Reduction between actuator output and joint motion, as a multiplier on torque. Efficiency is NOT modelled, so a derived capacity using this is an upper bound and must be labelled one (ADR-0004).

mimic.description: This joint's value is a fixed function of another joint's: multiplier * other + offset. URDF's element, adopted verbatim (ADR-0008). It is how a parallel jaw gripper, a differential wrist, or a linkage driven by one actuator is expressed WITHOUT a loop in the graph — the coupling is kinematic, the topology is still a tree. The consequence that matters: a mimicking joint is NOT independently commandable, so a reachability computation must not sample it as a free axis. That is the whole reason it lives in the model rather than in a note. A validator rejects a mimic cycle, a mimic naming a joint that does not exist, and a mimic on or naming a fixed joint.

multiplier.description: Absent means 1, matching URDF's default. Unlike a limit, this default is safe: it is the identity, not a physical claim.

offset.description: Absent means 0, matching URDF. Radians for revolute, millimetres for prismatic, per the driven joint's type.

transform.description: A pose relative to the parent frame. Translation in millimetres, rotation as roll/pitch/yaw in radians (ADR-0005). Both default to zero when absent, which is the one safe default here: an omitted transform means the frames coincide, which is a statement, not a guess. The rotation is FIXED-AXIS roll-pitch-yaw applied in X, Y, Z order, right-handed — REP-103's third-preference representation, and URDF's. Stating it matters for the same reason ADR-0005 refuses DH: REP-103 discourages Euler angles precisely because there are 24 conventions and the numbers do not record which one they are, and rpy is one letter away from being that mistake. Lengths convert to URDF's metres by a factor of 1000 at exactly one boundary (ADR-0007).

source.description: Where the claim came from. Required on the robot and on every joint, because a joint limit is a physical claim about hardware and the platform gates those on citations. TODO(source) is an acceptable citation string and is expected to fail loudly downstream until replaced — that is what a placeholder is for.
